introduction: “The ones in real authority are known by their humility and self-sacrifice.” This guide follows the Spiritual Assembly from Bahá’u’lláh’s ordinance that “in every city in the world a house be established in the name of justice”, through ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s letters to the first Assemblies in Persia and America on who should serve, how they should be chosen and what they should do, to Shoghi Effendi’s and the Universal House of Justice’s statements that an Assembly consults and does not dictate, that its members are shepherds, and that over-administration is a danger. Moses and Jethro, the choosing of the seven and of Matthias, the council at Jerusalem and Proverbs’ “multitude of counsellors” are scripture’s experience of the same things; the Qur’an commends those who settle affairs by counsel. Aristotle, Pericles, Burke, Madison and Tocqueville speak from the history of self-government, and Mill for the individual whose rights reading 124 affirms. Martha’s busyness and Ezekiel’s self-feeding shepherds are the warnings.
questions: Reading 2 says real authority is known by humility. How would a community tell, in practice, whether its institutions have that character?
Compare the qualities asked of Assembly members with Jethro’s “able men” and the seven “of honest report”. What is constant across three thousand years?
Burke says a representative owes his judgment, not obedience to his electors’ opinion. Is a Bahá’í Assembly member in the same position?
Readings 59 and 124 pull different ways on individual opinion. State the balance the guide strikes, and test it against Mill.
“Think of conveying the message, and not of the formation of committees.” When does administration serve the purpose and when does it replace it?
Madison wanted government obliged to control itself. What safeguards against misuse of authority do readings 123 to 131 describe?

outside.why: Assemblies as the most effective instrument of unity. Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
Those in real authority are known by humility and self-sacrifice. Whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.
The scene behind the saying: Jesus washing his disciples’ feet, and Peter’s protest.
Many assemblies are formed in the world; this one is different. Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

An Assembly established to promote the common good. Tocqueville on a people’s habit: Americans of all ages, all conditions, and all dispositions, constantly form associations. What distinguishes a Spiritual Assembly from a voluntary association?
Aided by the Spirit of God. The first Christian council wrote: it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us.
In every city a house of justice where the trusted gather. Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
The council of the Haudenosaunee under its Tree of the Great Peace, whose roots spread to the four directions, is an older assembly of the same hope.
Every assembly needs seasoned and worthy members. Jethro’s advice to Moses: provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness.
The elected must be righteous, God-fearing, incorruptible. Look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom.
Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.
News of an election. The first choosing of an officer in the church: they prayed, and gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias.
“There are no offices in this Cause.” One is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.
A community of cooperative servants with no leader but God. As the body is one, and hath many members, so also is Christ.
A duty laid on the Assembly as obligatory. If ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
Do not entrust orphans’ funds to one individual. Give unto orphans their wealth; absorb not their wealth into your own.
Income and expenditure managed by an agreed centre. He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
Paul’s word for those who hold what is not their own: let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.
Unsigned and unsealed documents are not to be trusted. The salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle.
Members must keep confidences. A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
The spread of the Word is obligatory; internal management comes second. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations.
Importance given to the women’s teaching assembly. I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church.
A divine gathering that shares the work. Moses: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.

“Think of conveying the message, and not of the formation of committees.” Martha was cumbered about much serving, and was told that one thing is needful. How does a community keep its administration from crowding out its purpose?
The beginning of organization. Let all things be done decently and in order.

Every fifty or hundred to elect one, and these to elect the body. Jethro’s scheme of rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens began with: the thing that thou doest is not good; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

Are affairs in the hands of the Assembly or of the people? Aristotle on why the many may judge better than the few: a feast to which many contribute is better than a dinner provided out of a single purse.

The Convention is like a parliament; the delegates represent the whole body. Burke to his electors: your representative owes you, not his industry only, but his judgment; and he betrays, instead of serving you, if he sacrifices it to your opinion. What do Bahá’í electors owe those they elect, and the elected their electors?
Obedience to the consultative assembly is binding. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.

“It should not be that each person follows their own opinion.” Mill: over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign. Reading 124 itself speaks of “the undoubted right of the individual to self-expression”. Where do the readings draw the line between the two?
Organizational matters settled by the counsels given. The Qur’an praises those whose affairs are a matter of counsel.
Consult with the Chicago House of Spirituality. Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
Read this letter in the Assembly and decide. The apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.
Let the Assembly keep affairs flowing and leave Him free. Moses was told to lay his hand on Joshua, and put some of his honour upon him.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá in constant communication with any Assembly established in unity. He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit.
No edifice stands without a firm foundation. Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.
May that gathering become a lamp. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
May this new assembly cause a brilliant light to shine. Arise, shine; for thy light is come.
“I have brought you the sand, the mortar, the bricks and the stone. You must build.” Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
Counsellors to the number of Bahá in every city. Paul’s list for an overseer: blameless, vigilant, sober, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not greedy of filthy lucre.
Local Assemblies are newly born, struggling to establish themselves. For who hath despised the day of small things?

The difficult art of consultation. Pericles of Athens: regarding him who takes no part in these duties not as unambitious but as useless, we Athenians are able to judge at all events if we cannot originate; we think discussion an indispensable preliminary to any wise action.
A sacred obligation to help, advise, protect and guide. Bear ye one another’s burdens.
The primary purpose is to promote teaching. The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
“The undoubted right of the individual to self-expression.” Milton: let Truth and Falsehood grapple; who ever knew Truth put to the worse, in a free and open encounter?
Their function is not to dictate but to consult. Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him; and the kingdom divided.
Administrators must be like shepherds. Woe be to the shepherds that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?
He shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.
Over-administration can be worse than too little. They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders.
Authority tempered to the gravity of each case. To do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.

Neither the individual left wholly to himself nor wholly controlled. Madison on the same balance: you must first enable the government to control the governed; and in the next place oblige it to control itself. What in the Bahá’í arrangement obliges an Assembly to control itself?

shortfall: Stretches three and five to eight are largely ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s letters to particular Assemblies: congratulations on being formed, practical instructions, greetings. They were left with few companions, and those given go to the principles of membership, election, consultation and service.
